fields.description: The date the product was approved as stated in the FDA approval letter to the applicant.
Products approved prior to the January 1, 1982 contain the phrase: "Approved prior to Jan 1, 1982".
Code to designate exclusivity granted by the FDA to a drug product.
The definition of the exclusivity code.
The date the exclusivity expires.
Patents submitted on FDA Form 3542 and listed after August 18, 2003 may have a drug product flag indicating the sponsor submitted the patent as claiming the drug product.
Patents submitted on FDA Form 3542 and listed after August 18, 2003 may have a drug substance flag indicating the sponsor submitted the patent as claiming the drug substance.
The date the patent expires as submitted by the applicant holder including applicable extensions.
The flag is set to 'Y' when an applicant holder has requested a patent to be delisted but the patent cannot be delisted.

Patent numbers as submitted by the applicant holder for patents covered by the statutory provisions. May repeat for multiple applications and multiple products. Includes pediatric exclusivity granted by the agency.
The date on which the FDA receives patent information from the applicant holder. Patent submission date data is included for patents submitted after 2013.
A code to designate a method of use that covers the approved indication or use of a drug product.
The definition of the patent use code.
The FDA assigned number to identify the application products. Each strength is a separate product. May repeat for multiple part products.
The names of the active, medicinal ingredients in the drug product.
The strength of the active, medicinal ingredients in the drug product.
The full name of the firm holding legal responsibility for the new drug application.
Name of the Applicant for the drug product.
The FDA assigned number to the application.
The type of new drug application approval.
Brand or trade name of the drug product.
The drug’s dosage form. There is no standard, but values may include terms like `tablet` or `solution for injection`.
The group or category of approved drugs.

The RLD is a drug product approved under section 505(c) of the FD&C Act for which FDA has made a finding of safety and effectiveness. In the electronic Orange Book, an RLD is identified by “RLD” in the RLD column.
A highly purified compound that is well characterized.
The route of administration of the drug product.
